findings: Shared BaseGun use-tick method calls virtual fireGun and only enters success handling when it returns true
Successful server-player path invokes doRecoil after damage/stat/cooldown handling
GunRecoilPacket serializes only recoilAmount float and firingTime int
Packet has no weapon-instance ID, hand, configuration revision or shot ordinal
The inspected doRecoil path sends to the firing player, not an identified observer/tracking broadcast
The client packet handler calls ClientOperations.addRecoil; treating this as a complete animation identity event is unsafe after swaps/offhand changes
proposal: Preserve existing server firing and resource semantics. Bind the existing ConfirmedShotPresentation core to a genuinely authoritative identity-bearing event; do not reconstruct identity from recoil amplitude or the currently held item. Prediction and observer routing remain separate native work.
